questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: The history of New Year celebrations around the world
Why people drink, and trying to stop drinking for a month
How to run a successful campaign on social media
The best ways to cure a hangover
questions.why: Sam and Rob discuss Dry January and why it is hard to give up alcohol.

questions.q: How did Rob do with his New Year's resolutions?
options: He kept all of them
He kept the running one but not the others
He didn't make any this year
He broke all of them after a few days
questions.why: Rob says he failed on all of them and only lasted a few days.

options: Not drinking alcohol
Having no rain in January
Eating no sweet food
Spending no money
questions.why: Rob explains that 'dry' refers to not drinking alcohol, not the weather.

options: A doctor who studies the effects of alcohol on health
A journalist who presents a health show on BBC Radio 4
The founder of a group called The Sober Girl Society
A shop owner who sells Christmas jumpers in London
questions.why: Rob introduces her as the founder of The Sober Girl Society.

questions.q: According to Millie, why is it hard to stop drinking?
options: Alcohol is cheaper than soft drinks in most pubs and bars
Friends expect it, and alcohol is on products everywhere
Doctors say a small glass of wine a day is good for you
Bars stay open very late in the UK, even on weeknights
questions.why: She mentions peer pressure and alcohol jokes on jumpers and birthday cards.

questions.q: Why did Millie finally decide to give up alcohol?
options: It made her anxious and affected her daily life
Her friends and family kept asking her to stop
She was drinking every single day, even at work
She could no longer afford to buy drinks when out
questions.why: She says alcohol was affecting her mental health, with hangover anxiety spreading into everyday life.

questions.q: How does Millie describe her own drinking?
options: She drank a small amount every evening
She only drank at work events
She drank heavily now and then, not every day
She drank only at Christmas
questions.why: She says she was a binge drinker rather than an everyday drinker.

questions.q: Why does Millie mention the Christmas jumpers and birthday cards?
options: To recommend them as gifts
To show that she makes this merchandise
To complain that they are too expensive
To show how common jokes about drinking are
questions.why: She uses them as examples of how alcohol is 'absolutely everywhere' and hard to avoid.
